fees.note: Two people: $20. There is no camping fee here; what it costs is Montana FWP's Conservation License, which everyone 12 or older needs to use a fishing access site: $10 per non-resident, so $20 for two. It is an annual license (March 1 to the end of February), so it also covers every other night at Montana fishing access sites and wildlife areas that license year. Residents pay $8 (youth 12-17 and seniors 62+ $4); anyone with a Montana fishing license already has one, and under-12s need none. Buy it online at ols.fwp.mt.gov, at an FWP office or from a license agent. (AWH 2026-10-11: price as two people, one night.)

It is an annual license (March 1 to the end of February), so it also covers every other night at Montana fishing access sites and wildlife areas that license year. Residents pay $8 (youth 12-17 and seniors 62+ $4); anyone with a Montana fishing license already has one, and under-12s need none. Buy it online at ols.fwp.mt.gov, at an FWP office or from a license agent. (AWH 2026-10-11: price as two people, one night.)

source: https://myfwp.mt.gov/fishMT/fas/39754405 ('Facilities & Fees' lists only the Conservation License: MT resident $8, senior 62+/youth 12-17 $4, nonresident $10; no camping fee) and https://fwp.mt.gov/buyandapply/conservation-license (everyone 12+ needs one to access fishing access sites; license year from March 1); two people, one night per AWH 2026-10-11
